entries.claim: In the United States, iOS accounted for about 60.7% and Android about 39.3% of mobile page views in August 2026.

facts.of: iOS share of US mobile OS page views

entries.appliesWhen: Web page-view share; not installed base, downloads or spend.

support.excerpt: iOS: 60.68%, Android: 39.29%, period August 2026, based on page views

entries.useFor: US is iOS-majority in traffic: give App Store creative equal weight to Play.
entries.researcherNote: Single independent source found; the search tool budget was exhausted so a second independent origin (Counterpoint, Comscore, Sensor Tower) could not be added. Page-view methodology overstates iOS relative to device counts in some markets.

entries.claim: In a published SplitMetrics test on Angry Birds 2 (App Store), portrait screenshots outperformed landscape at 99.7% confidence.
entries.appliesWhen: Casual game, App Store, single vendor case.

support.excerpt: Portrait-oriented screenshots outperformed landscape, contrary to industry standards ... 99.7% confidence level on portrait orientation test

entries.validFor: Test date not stated on the page (Angry Birds 2 launch period)
entries.useFor: Do not assume landscape wins for games; test orientation for the roguelike audience.
entries.researcherNote: Country of test not stated (filed under US baseline by earlier work). Vendor case study of its own customer; casual audience, not roguelike. One case = one origin.

entries.claim: AppsFlyer advises keeping screenshot text to about four or five words per line, because users will not enlarge screenshots to read.
entries.appliesWhen: Vendor advice for App Store screenshots.

support.excerpt: keep text to just four or five words per line

entries.useFor: Short captions; treat as a starting rule, test it.

entries.claim: Phiture research, cited by AppsFlyer, found 17% of users scroll through screenshots for games versus 9% for apps overall.
entries.appliesWhen: Second-hand statistic; date and country of the study not shown.

support.excerpt: Only 9% of app users scroll through screenshots vs. 17% for games (Phiture research cited)

entries.useFor: Most users see only the first screenshots; games get somewhat more scrolling.
entries.researcherNote: Original Phiture study not read; store not specified.

entries.claim: SplitMetrics states that users typically decide whether to download within 7 seconds of visiting a product page.

support.excerpt: Users typically make download decisions within 7 seconds of visiting a product page
The 7-second data is cited to Phiture research

entries.validFor: App Store Connect / Apple Developer pages as of 2026-09
entries.researcherNote: Provenance unclear: AppsFlyer attributes a 7-second figure to Phiture; SplitMetrics gives no dataset.

entries.claim: Phiture advises treating screenshot captions as keyword-aware content while warning that keyword-stuffed screenshots look desperate and convert poorly.

support.excerpt: Treat screenshot captions as keyword-aware content. That means keyword-stuffed screenshots look desperate and convert poorly.

entries.researcherNote: Depends on the unproven caption-indexing claim (see ap-070).

entries.claim: SplitMetrics advises that for games, actual gameplay in previews is essential to conversion.

support.excerpt: For games specifically, actual gameplay previews are essential for positively impacting conversion rates.

entries.validFor: App Store Connect / Apple Developer pages as of 2026-09
entries.useFor: Show real gameplay in the App Store preview.
entries.researcherNote: Consistent with Apple guidance (ap-025); vendor origin only.
